title: Binary Tree Postorder Traversal
description:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the **postorder traversal** of its nodes' values.

In a postorder traversal, you visit the left subtree first, then the right subtree, and finally the current node (Left -> Right -> Root). If the tree is empty (`root` is `null`), return an empty list.
hints: Recursively visit `node.left`, then `node.right`, and append `node.val` last.
For an iterative approach, notice that reversing a modified preorder traversal (Root -> Right -> Left) gives Left -> Right -> Root.
Alternatively, track the last visited node on a single explicit stack so you only pop a parent after its right subtree has been processed.

examples.explanation: Visit left of 1 (none), go right to 2, visit left child 3, right of 2 (none), then 2, and finally 1 -> [3, 2, 1].
Visiting Left -> Right -> Root across every subtree produces [4, 6, 7, 5, 2, 9, 8, 3, 1].
An empty tree produces an empty list.
